subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the Rover K-Series across its 1 model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The Rover K-Series is fitted across Freelander — we see it regularly across the full application range.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Bearings, timing chain components, gaskets, and twin-scroll turbocharger components as standard. We also inspect and measure the cylinder head, crankshaft, and other critical components.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: No widely-reported failure pattern is confirmed for the Rover K-Series across its applications. We don't treat this engine as having one universal failure mode; diagnosis is required to establish whether an engine needs repair, rebuild, or replacement.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page — they'll be added once a documented set of completed Rover K-Series rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.

typical.title: LAND ROVER Rover K-Series REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: A full Rover K-Series rebuild involves stripping the engine down, inspecting the crankshaft, cylinder head and timing components, and replacing worn bearings, gaskets and seals with updated OEM-specification parts (Inline-4 (I4), 1.8L (1,796 cc), Petrol).

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing chain, bearings, gaskets, twin-scroll turbocharger inspection/refurbishment, calibration of fuel injection system
